summary: Ash buys three tamales from Pilar, paying from his left pocket in a ritualized, wordless transaction.
location: Corner of Pershing and the old rail spur, Waukegan
object: Φ12 coins, tamales wrapped in banana leaf and foil
consequence: Establishes Ash's presence in Waukegan and his routine before heading to the shrine

summary: Ash arrives at the unofficial roadside shrine on his walk north.
location: Shrine at the broken signal post, Waukegan
object: Wooden board nailed to a signal post
consequence: Sets up the ritual of naming the dead and the emotional weight that follows

summary: Ash pours two fingers of filtered lake water into the ceramic cup at the shrine as an offering.
location: Shrine at the broken signal post, Waukegan
consequence: Initiates the naming ritual and signals Ash's sense of obligation to the dead

summary: Ash says the names of the dead aloud — his grandmother's first, then three others — but deliberately omits a fourth name.
location: Shrine at the broken signal post, Waukegan
consequence: The withheld fourth name becomes a source of unresolved emotional tension that disrupts his routine

summary: Ash recites his memorized route from Waukegan to Kenosha under his breath, performing his internal navigation ritual.
location: Shrine at the broken signal post, Waukegan
consequence: Demonstrates Ash's identity as a courier and his method of grounding himself, which then fails

summary: Ash stops reciting and lingers at the shrine four minutes longer than usual, his hand resting on the wooden board, unable to move on.
location: Shrine at the broken signal post, Waukegan
consequence: Signals that the unspoken fourth name is actively destabilizing Ash's composure and forward momentum

summary: It is confirmed that there is a fourth name Ash chose not to say at the shrine.
location: Shrine at the broken signal post, Waukegan
consequence: Establishes a central unresolved mystery — who the fourth person is and why Ash cannot or will not name them

summary: Ash discovers the tamales are cold before he even lifts the cloth, confirming he arrived late or they were left long ago.
consequence: Establishes Ash's displacement in time and place, his transience

summary: Ash eats the cold tamales standing, refusing to sit as a deliberate act of non-belonging.
consequence: Reveals Ash's psychological code around impermanence and rootlessness

summary: Ash leaves offerings at the shrine and performs his forty-seventh marking ritual at a shrine between Waukegan and the Kenosha Crossing.
location: shrine in former lakeshore processing shed, Waukegan
object: bottle cap, dried seed pod, folded paper with a route written on it
consequence: Establishes Ash's private system of navigation and meaning-making across a long journey

summary: Ash recites a route from memory under his breath while eating, encoding waypoint knowledge as oral tradition.
consequence: Reveals the nature of Ash's expertise and the unreliability of maps in this world

summary: A young stranger appears in the doorway holding an unidentified cloth-wrapped object, watching Ash without hiding or threatening.
location: doorway of former lakeshore processing shed, Waukegan
consequence: Interrupts Ash's ritual and introduces an unknown threat or complication

summary: Ash observes that the boy's scarification marks are incomplete — half a set, freshly keloid, suggesting an interrupted or unfinished rite.
location: doorway of former lakeshore processing shed, Waukegan
consequence: Signals the boy's ambiguous or liminal social status within whatever marking culture exists here

summary: The boy speaks a name at Ash — a name that has not been used in eleven years and that the boy should not know.
consequence: Shatters Ash's anonymity and raises urgent questions about who sent the boy and what they want

summary: The boy leaves silently, taking the cloth-wrapped object with him.
consequence: Ash registers the departure as unresolved; the object's contents and the boy's purpose remain unknown

summary: Ash watches the empty doorway and drops his hand from his synthetic eye.
consequence: Establishes Ash's habit of marking and cataloguing unresolved situations

summary: Ash and Brisa walk north together without explanation.
consequence: Establishes their professional dynamic and shared operational discipline

summary: Ash recites the Iron Bend checkpoint mnemonic under his breath while walking.
consequence: Reveals Ash's operational knowledge of northern routes and checkpoint protocols

summary: Brisa asks how long it took Ash to learn all the checkpoint mnemonics.
consequence: Opens a guarded exchange that reveals shared history and mutual assessment between the two

summary: Ash reveals that someone taught him the northern routes and the particular habits of inspectors, without naming who.
consequence: Implies a significant unnamed mentor or contact; creates a silence that functions as a shared boundary neither character crosses

summary: Brisa describes a specific residential block in Escanaba — twelve stories, poured concrete, 340 units — and its blast radius as a problem she would have faced if called for the job.
consequence: Reveals Brisa's demolitions expertise and implies she was considered for — but not given — a destructive operation near civilian population

summary: Ash identifies the smell of the package under his coat as the interior of a lived-in building.
consequence: The domestic quality of the package's smell takes on significance; Ash chooses not to voice it, marking it internally
